assumption: TIV recomputed as floor_area × cost_per_m2 (rounded KES 5,000); file column is 10× the documented value.
Quality index = position of cost_per_m2 within the published cost band of the class.
Area labels and LLM geocoding use approximate town centroids (±2–3 km).
Building depth = depth of the containing 925 m JRC cell (point sampling). Bilinear sampling reported as sensitivity.
No flooding at RP ≤ 2 (in-bank flow); depth linear in ln(RP) between published maps.
Beyond RP500 depth extrapolated with the RP200→500 slope, capped at RP10,000.
Shape from JRC/Huizinga (2017) Africa residential curve; global residential used as secondary source.
Class plinth heights, depth multipliers and ceilings (75–95%) are expert judgement.
ML model trained on 30,000 synthetic pseudo-claims; it reproduces the encoded assumptions plus their uncertainty, not real claims experience.
Flood duration default 7 days (Budalangi floods often stand for 1–3 weeks).
Each JRC map treated as one basin-wide event (full spatial correlation of hazard).
Illustrative terms: 2% TIV deductible, 100% limit, Cat XL KES 20M xs 20M, no quota share.
One dominant river flood per year (annual maximum); AEP = OEP.
Secondary uncertainty correlated across buildings with a Gaussian copula, ρ = 0.3.
Losses cover the structure only — no contents, business interruption, or demand surge.
